text: A group consists of a set G with a binary operation that is associative, has an identity element e acting on both sides, and gives every element of G a two-sided inverse.

editorial_note: Independently authored mathematical paraphrase of the direct source; unsealed, not third-party peer reviewed. The source also offers an equivalence with the centre of G; the elementary commutativity test is the present candidate.
text: An abelian group is a group G whose binary operation is commutative: for every a,b in G, ab = ba.

editorial_note: Independently authored mathematical paraphrase of the direct source; unsealed, not third-party peer reviewed. Retain the distinction between one-sided and two-sided ideals in noncommutative rings.
text: A two-sided ideal I of a ring R is an additive subgroup of R with r i and i r in I for every r in R and i in I; over commutative rings left and right ideals coincide.

editorial_note: Independently authored mathematical paraphrase of the direct source; unsealed, not third-party peer reviewed. Properness is essential; source includes other equivalent tests, not assumed in this candidate.
text: In a commutative ring R with identity, a prime ideal P is a proper ideal such that for all a,b in R, ab in P implies a in P or b in P.

editorial_note: Independently authored mathematical paraphrase of the direct source; unsealed, not third-party peer reviewed. The cited ProofWiki entry does NOT impose unitality universally; preserve the optional convention instead of silently imposing 1m=m.
text: A left R-module is an abelian group M with a left action R times M to M that distributes over each additive variable and obeys (rs)m = r(sm); if a unital module is intended, add 1m = m as a separate hypothesis.

editorial_note: Independently authored mathematical paraphrase of the direct source; unsealed, not third-party peer reviewed. The source presents topology on a set and its open-set axioms; the empty space is permitted by this axiom formulation.
text: A topological space is a pair (X,tau) where tau is a collection of subsets of X containing the empty set and X and closed under arbitrary unions and finite intersections; the elements of tau are the open sets.
